text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"Los Angeles","level":"city","category":"just_cause_eviction","status":"in_force","title":"Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)","requirement":"Landlords may not terminate a tenancy without just cause. At-fault causes include failure to cure a lease violation and creating a nuisance or causing damage. No-fault causes include owner or immediate family move-in, a resident manager moving in where required by law or an affordable housing covenant, demolition, permanent removal from the rental market or conversion to non-residential use, a government order to vacate, HUD selling the property, and conversion or demolition of a residential hotel. Relocation assistance is required for no-fault evictions and is not owed for at-fault evictions. The JCO applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
